title: Atomic staircase
story: A strontium titanate (SrTiO3) crystal baked at 1000 °C for an hour. Its surface atoms settle into flat terraces, and each step down is about one crystal unit (0.39 nm) tall. Scientists grow superconducting FeSe films on surfaces like this.

title: Superconductor city blocks
story: An 11 nm film of iron selenide (FeSe), a superconductor: cooled below about 8 kelvin (−265 °C) it carries electricity with zero resistance. Its crystals grow as square blocks because FeSe atoms sit on a square grid. A thin FeTe cap protects it from air.

title: Triangle pyramids
story: Bismuth selenide (Bi2Se3), a topological insulator: its inside blocks electricity but its surface conducts. Its atoms form a hexagonal pattern, so crystals grow as stacked triangles. Each step is one five-atom-thick layer, about 0.95 nm.

title: Terraced triangles
story: Indium selenide (InSe) grown on a 3-inch silicon wafer. Look for triangles stacked like wedding-cake tiers; every tier is roughly one InSe layer, about 0.8 nm tall.

title: Tin selenide honeycomb
story: Tin selenide (SnSe) grown on magnesium oxide. SnSe can turn heat into electricity. The scientists changed how much selenium they supplied and used AFM to see how the grains changed.

title: Islands on a sapphire sea
story: Tungsten disulfide (WS2) islands grown for 10 minutes on sapphire. The dark gaps are bare sapphire that the film has not covered yet. What fraction is covered?

title: Triangles, with a glitch
story: Tiny triangles of tungsten diselenide (WSe2), a semiconductor that could make transistors thinner than any silicon one. This scan also has a glitch from the microscope itself. Can you find it?

title: Smooth MoS2 carpet
story: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) grown for 3 minutes on sapphire. MoS2 is a leading candidate for ultra-thin computer-chip transistors: one layer is only about 0.65 nm thick.

title: Gallium selenide bumps
story: Gallium selenide (GaSe) grown on gallium arsenide at 400 °C for 40 minutes. GaSe can change the colour of laser light. Here it grew as rounded mounds instead of flat sheets.

title: Memory material
story: Indium selenide (In2Se3) on silicon. In2Se3 is ferroelectric: it can hold an electric 'up' or 'down' state without power, which could make memory chips that remember when switched off.

title: Almost perfectly flat
story: Tin telluride (SnTe) grown on indium phosphide. Its surface is so flat that the typical bump is about 0.36 nm, roughly the width of two atoms.

title: Magnet grains
story: A film from a study of chromium antimonide (CrSb), a magnetic material, grown by molecular beam epitaxy. The sample record lists two materials, CrSb and Sb2Te3. Its surface is covered in small rounded grains.
